extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and peer reviewers of biomedical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and recommendations for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and editing manuscripts for biomedical journals, including ethical principles (authorship, conflicts of interest, confidentiality), editorial policies, and technical manuscript formatting. Intended to guide authors, editors, and reviewers to produce accurate, clear, and ethically sound reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship credit criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship credit should be based on 1) substantial contributions to conception and design, or acquisition of data, or analysis and interpretation of data; 2) drafting the article or revising it critically for important intellectual content; and 3) final approval of the version to be published. Authors should meet conditions 1, 2, and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All persons designated as authors should qualify for authorship, and all who qualify should be listed. Each author should have participated sufficiently in the work to take public responsibility for appropriate portions of the content. Order of authorship should be a joint decision of the co-authors and be explainable. Journals are encouraged to develop contributorship and guarantorship policies; guarantors may be identified who take responsibility for integrity of the work as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group authorship and identification of responsible individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: When a large, multi-center group has conducted the work, the group should identify the individuals who accept direct responsibility for the manuscript; these individuals should fully meet authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author should indicate preferred citation, identify all individual authors and group name. Journals will generally list other group members in acknowledgments. The National Library of Medicine indexes group name and names of individuals identified as directly responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors listed in acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: All contributors who do not meet criteria for authorship should be listed in an acknowledgments section, with their contributions described (e.g., ‘provided technical help,’ ‘collected data’). Financial and material support should also be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups of contributors may be listed under headings such as ‘clinical investigators’ with function described. Because readers may infer endorsement, all persons must give written permission to be acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and responsibility of the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor is the person responsible for the entire content of the journal and must have full authority for determining editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should have direct access to highest level of ownership, a contract stating rights and duties and mechanisms for resolving conflict, and may use an independent editorial advisory board to help establish policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial freedom/independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors-in-chief should have full authority over editorial content; journal owners should not interfere in evaluation, selection, or editing of individual articles or create environments that strongly influence decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be based on validity and importance to readers, not commercial success. Editors should be free to express critical but responsible views about medicine without fear of retribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review as critical assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the critical assessment of manuscripts by experts not part of the editorial staff; it helps editors decide suitability and helps improve quality of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and kind of manuscripts sent for review, number of reviewers, procedures, and use of reviewers' opinions may vary. In the interests of transparency, journals should publicly disclose their peer review policies in instructions to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conflicts of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants in writing, peer review, and editorial decision making must disclose relationships that could be viewed as presenting a potential conflict of interest (financial or personal relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is important for authors, reviewers, and editors; editors may use disclosed information as a basis for decisions and should publish it if important for judging the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts related to individual authors' commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a manuscript, authors are responsible for disclosing all financial and personal relationships that might bias their work and must state explicitly whether potential conflicts do or do not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure should be on a conflict of interest notification page following the title page, with additional detail in a cover letter if necessary. Investigators must disclose potential conflicts to study participants and state whether they have done so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts related to project support (sponsors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should describe the role of study sponsors in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, writing, and decision to submit; if sponsor had no involvement, authors should state so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should not enter agreements that interfere with access to data or ability to publish. Editors may request authors funded by interested agencies to sign statements of data access and responsibility, review protocols/contracts, and may decline articles if sponsor asserts control over authors’ right to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts related to editors, journal staff, or reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should avoid selecting external reviewers with obvious conflicts; reviewers must disclose conflicts to editors and disqualify themselves if appropriate; editors making final decisions must have no personal, professional, or financial involvement in matters they judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may suggest who should not review and should explain concerns when possible. Editorial staff participating in decisions must disclose financial interests and disqualify themselves where conflicted. Reviewers must not use knowledge of unpublished work for personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy of patients and study participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Patients have a right to privacy that should not be infringed without informed consent; identifying information should not be published unless essential and with written informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informed consent for identifiable patients requires showing the manuscript to the patient. Masking eye region is inadequate. If identifying characteristics are altered, authors should assure alterations do not distort scientific meaning and editors should note that. Requirement for informed consent should be in journal instructions and indicated in the published article when obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality for authors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be reviewed with respect for authors' confidentiality; editors must not disclose information about manuscripts to anyone other than authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should treat manuscripts as privileged communications, not publicly discuss or appropriate ideas before publication, not make copies for personal files, and should return or destroy copies after review. Reviewer comments should not be published without permission of reviewer, author, and editor. Some journals publish reviews only with consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of human subjects and animals
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting experiments on human subjects, authors should indicate whether procedures followed were in accordance with institutional/national responsible committees and the Helsinki Declaration; if doubt exists, authors must explain rationale and show institutional approval. For animal experiments, indicate adherence to institutional and national guides for care and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should request such statements and rationale if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to consider publication of negative studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should seriously consider for publication any carefully done study relevant to readers whether results are negative or positive; failure to publish negative studies contributes to publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many negative studies are inconclusive; publication of inconclusive studies is problematic as they add little and consume resources. The Cochrane Library may be interested in publishing inconclusive trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections, retractions, and expressions of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors requiring correction should be published as corrections/errata on a numbered page, listed in contents, include the complete original citation, and link to the original article. If substantial doubts about honesty arise, editors should ensure appropriate investigation and publish retractions or expressions of concern as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction should explain why the article is retracted and include full original citation. Retractions/expressions should appear prominently and be properly labeled, and editors may request institutions to assure validity of previous work by authors of fraudulent papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright policy clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should make their position on copyright transfer clear to authors; many journals ask authors to transfer copyright while some open-access journals do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright status can vary; editors should communicate rights and any permitted uses (serial rights, government-authored content exceptions, waivers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Most biomedical journals will not consider manuscripts simultaneously being considered by other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist when simultaneous publication is jointly decided for public health reasons. Authors should not submit the same manuscript to multiple journals concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant (duplicate) publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundant publication is publication that overlaps substantially with one already published. Most journals do not wish to receive papers that have been largely reported elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must fully disclose all submissions and previous reports that might be regarded as redundant. Copies of related material should accompany submissions. If redundant publication occurs without notification, expect editorial action (at least rejection) and possible notices of redundant publication if already published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable secondary publication conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary publication (e.g., guidelines or translations) is acceptable provided specific conditions are met: approval from both journals' editors; respect primary publication priority; intended for different readers; faithful reflection of data and interpretations; footnote informing readers of primary reference; title indicates secondary publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority should be respected by an interval of at least one week unless negotiated. Permission for secondary publication should be free of charge. National Library of Medicine does not consider translations to be 'republications' for indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling competing manuscripts from same study (differences in analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If coworkers submit competing manuscripts that differ in analysis or interpretation, authors should submit manuscripts that clearly present both versions and explain differences in a cover letter; peer/editorial review may help resolve disagreement, and if unresolved, both versions or a single paper with two analyses may be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor may publish a statement outlining the disagreement and the journal’s role in attempts to resolve it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling competing manuscripts from same study (differences in methods or results)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dispute centers on differing opinions about what was actually done or observed, the editor should refuse publication until the disagreement is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review cannot be expected to resolve such disputes. If allegations of dishonesty or fraud arise, editors should inform appropriate authorities and notify authors of intention to report suspected misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing manuscripts based on the same database
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should consider duplicate or competing manuscripts based on the same database carefully (text indicates guidance continues beyond excerpt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose related submissions and prior reports; editors may request additional information to decide how to handle competing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to register clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals have an obligation to require registration of clinical trials (listed as a section heading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trial registration policies and requirements should be stated by journals (document references registration obligation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation — general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Uniform Requirements provide recommendations for specific elements of editing and writing to improve quality and clarity of reporting in manuscripts; authors should follow recommendations where possible but also consult journal-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are based on shared experience and accompanied by rationale. Authors should learn journal-specific policies (suitable topics, article types) and follow them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for specific study designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow reporting guidelines appropriate for the study design (e.g., CONSORT for randomized controlled trials) and provide requested checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many journals require completion of checklists for certain study types; authors should consult journal instructions and send checklists if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should include a title page containing required information (section heading for Title page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specific elements vary by journal, title page typically contains title, author names and affiliations, corresponding author contact, and may be accompanied by conflict of interest notification page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest notification page (manuscript placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must state conflicts of interest on a conflict of interest notification page that follows the title page in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide additional detail in a cover letter if necessary. Editors may publish disclosed information when important for judging the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must include an abstract and key words (section heading present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals vary in abstract style (structured vs unstructured); authors should consult target journal for format and length and include key words for indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion (IMRAD) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should present Introduction, Methods (including selection/description of participants, technical information, statistics), Results, and Discussion sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should provide sufficient detail for reproducibility; statistics section should identify methods and measures; Results should present data clearly; Discussion should interpret findings and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and description of participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should clearly describe selection and characteristics of study participants (heading: Selection and Description of Participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment methods, and relevant demographic/clinical characteristics to allow readers to judge applicability and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical information and statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical details and statistical methods should be described sufficiently for replication and assessment of validity (headings: Technical Information; Statistics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify statistical measures of variation (SD, SEM), state statistical tests, and explain nonstandard procedures. Editors may request additional details or raw data when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: References — general considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using abstracts as references; provide direct references to original research when possible; cite accepted but unpublished papers as 'in press' and verify acceptance and obtain permission; cite 'unpublished observations' with written permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should verify references against original documents to minimize citation errors. Small numbers of key references are often preferable to exhaustive lists; electronic versions allow supplementary references.

rubrics_metrics.name: References — style and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Uniform Requirements style is based on an ANSI standard adapted by the NLM. References should be numbered consecutively in order of first mention; identify references by Arabic numerals in parentheses; journal titles abbreviated per Index Medicus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult National Library of Medicine for sample formats. Authors should consult target journal about electronic reference citation preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables — formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be typed/printed double spaced on separate sheets, numbered consecutively, given brief titles, without internal horizontal or vertical lines, with short column headings and explanatory matter in footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain nonstandard abbreviations in footnotes using specified symbol sequence; identify statistical measures of variation; ensure each table is cited in text. Additional extensive backup tables may be published electronically and should be submitted for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations (figures) — quality and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be professionally drawn/photographed or high-quality digital prints; provide version suitable for printing and electronic web formats. For diagnostic images and photomicrographs send sharp prints; letters/numbers/symbols must be legible when reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide internal scale markers for photomicrographs; symbols should contrast with background. Obtain written permission to publish photographs of identifiable people; acknowledge and obtain permission for previously published figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends for illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Legends should be typed double spaced on a separate page with Arabic numerals corresponding to illustrations; explain symbols, arrows, internal scale, and staining methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and detailed explanations belong in legends, not on illustrations themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report measurements of length, height, weight, and volume in metric units (meter, kilogram, liter) or decimal multiples; temperatures in degrees Celsius; blood pressures in mm Hg unless journal requires other units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report laboratory information in both local and International System of Units (SI) when appropriate; editors may request alternative or non-SI units to be added before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only standard abbreviations; avoid abbreviations in the title. The full term should precede first use in text unless a standard unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-standard abbreviations can confuse readers; explain abbreviation on first use and in table/figure footnotes as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission and manuscript copies for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals accept electronic submission (disk, email attachment, website upload); electronic submission saves time and postage and allows handling in electronic form. If paper submission, send required number of copies for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting electronically, consult the journal's instructions. Authors should not expect editorial staff to make required copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter should accompany the manuscript and include: full statement about submissions/previous reports that might be redundant; statement of financial/other relationships that might lead to conflict; statement that manuscript has been read and approved by all authors and requirements for authorship have been met; name/address/phone of corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include additional helpful information (article type) and previous editors’ and reviewers’ comments and authors' responses if manuscript was previously submitted; copies of permissions to reproduce materials or use identifiable people must accompany the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission and study-type checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals provide pre-submission checklists to ensure all components are included; some require authors to complete checklists for certain study types (e.g., CONSORT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check whether the target journal uses such checklists and send them with the manuscript if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for reproduced material and identifiable people
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of permissions to reproduce published material, to use illustrations or report information about identifiable people, or to name people for their contributions must accompany the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission is required irrespective of authorship or publisher, except for public domain documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference accuracy verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should verify references against original documents to minimize citation errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some journals check accuracy of all references but not all do; verification reduces published citation errors.
